extracted.intended_audience: individual humanities scholars (including independent and junior scholars) preparing NEH Fellowships applications
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an application for an NEH Fellowship: an individual-scholar grant to support humanities research or creation of scholarly outputs (books, editions, digital resources, translations, articles). Includes eligibility, topic restrictions for 2026, required materials, and procedural steps (Grants.gov, letters of recommendation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Core quality standard: exceptional research, rigorous analysis, and clear writing
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH Fellowships are competitive awards granted to individual scholars pursuing projects that embody exceptional research, rigorous analysis, and clear writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should demonstrate high scholarly quality in research methods, analytical rigor, and prose clarity; these are the central evaluative hallmarks of meritorious proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Articulate project's value to humanities scholars and/or general audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must clearly articulate a project's value to humanities scholars, general audiences, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the contribution and audiences for the proposed work; make clear why the project matters and to whom (scholarly significance, public relevance, or both).

rubrics_metrics.name: 2026 topical eligibility: American history/culture and Western civilization
rubrics_metrics.description: The 2026 Fellowships competition will only accept projects for research in American history and culture and Western civilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competitive applications must focus on topics in the history, culture, and government of the United States (Colonial Era to present) or topics in Western civilization from antiquity to the present. Proposals outside these topic areas are ineligible for this cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable project outputs (expected deliverables)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships support time to conduct research or produce books, monographs, peer-reviewed articles, e-books, born-digital materials, translations with annotations or a critical apparatus, or critical editions resulting from previous research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List of expected outputs on the program page: Book; Critical Edition; Digital Resource or Publication; Other Scholarly Resource; Peer-reviewed Article; Translation with annotations or critical apparatus. Proposals should identify the expected product(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project stage flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects may be at any stage of development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may propose early-stage projects or work building on prior research; indicate stage and realistic plan for delivering the stated output within the fellowship period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible applicants and payment handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships are awards granted to individual scholars; NEH encourages submissions from independent scholars and junior scholars. Fellowship awards are paid directly to the applicant, not to their institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Independent scholars and early-career applicants are explicitly encouraged. Budget and payment arrangements assume direct payment to the individual grantee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and period limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum award amount $60,000 ($5,000 per month). Period of performance: six to twelve months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must conform to the maximum award and duration. Project start dates listed for the cycle (e.g., April 1, 2027 and September 1, 2028) should be observed when proposing timeline and budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: One application per applicant per deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: You can apply to only one program at each deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must choose a single NEH program to apply to in a given cycle; submitting multiple program applications at the same deadline is not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) and Program Announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the Notice of Funding Opportunity and the Program Announcement for Fellowships to ensure you understand all the expectations and restrictions for projects delivered under this program and are prepared to write an effective application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to NOFO instructions for eligibility, page limits, required attachments, formats, and any restrictions. The program announcement contains essential requirements that determine completeness and eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use provided application materials and samples cautiously
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample Application Narratives are provided to give applicants a sense of how a successful application might be crafted but are not intended to serve as models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that the format of older samples may have changed; follow the current NOFO precisely rather than mimicking sample formats. Use samples only for a general sense of content and level of detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov registration and submission procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Register for a Grants.gov account; add an 'individual applicant' profile; follow Grants.gov’s instructions for adding a profile; submit your application package on Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your Grants.gov account is current, add the correct profile type, download any required software (e.g., Adobe Reader), and follow the Grants.gov application package instructions. Register and complete profiles well before the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit and verify confirmations from Grants.gov and NEH
rubrics_metrics.description: You will receive a confirmation from Grants.gov when you’ve successfully submitted your application and up to five more notices confirming different stages in the application process; verify that you have received all confirmations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check spam/junk folders for confirmation emails. Only after final confirmation from Grants.gov and NEH should you assume the submission is complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of recommendation: timing, tracking, and applicant responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: NEH will request letters of reference from your recommenders approximately seven to ten days after the application deadline. You will be notified by email when each of your letters of reference has been received. You may check the status of the letters in NEH’s secure site and send reminders to letter writers; you are responsible for ensuring that your letter writers have received solicitations and submitted their letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor letter receipt via the secure NEH site (using NEH application number and Grants.gov tracking number). If necessary, remind recommenders and provide upload links; applicants bear responsibility for missing letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: NEH policy resources to consult (including AI policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program Resources include a Policy on the Use of Artificial Intelligence for NEH Grant Proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult NEH policies (including AI policy) when preparing application content and methodologies. Failure to follow NEH policies could affect eligibility or review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitiveness and program statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: In the last five competitions this program received an average of 1,033 applications per year and had a 7% funding ratio, with an average of 69 awards per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware of the program's competitiveness when planning submissions and may use these statistics to set expectations and craft particularly strong, distinctive proposals.
